name: workbuddy-anywhere-for-copilot
description: WorkBuddy Anywhere for Copilot: use WorkBuddy models in VS Code Chat, with hosted multi-account support and a management page shared with the desktop app

commands.title: WorkBuddy Anywhere: Manage Account
commands.description: Accounts, quota, packages, check-in, models and settings. Also what the status bar opens.

commands.title: WorkBuddy Anywhere: Manage Account (Global)
commands.description: The same management page, opened on the international cluster.

commands.title: WorkBuddy Anywhere: Menu
commands.description: Alias for the management page, kept so existing keybindings keep working.

commands.title: WorkBuddy Anywhere: Sign Out
commands.description: Opens the management page, where every account is listed with its quota.

commands.title: WorkBuddy Anywhere: Select Vision Fallback Model
commands.description: Opens the management page's Settings tab, where every chat model registered in VS Code's LM namespace is selectable.

codebuddy.thinkingEffort.description: Thinking/reasoning depth for models that support it

codebuddy.visionFallbackModel.description: Model used to describe images when the selected chat model doesn't accept images. Format: "vendor/model" for a VS Code LM model (e.g. "copilot/gpt-4o"). Empty = auto (VS Code models are tried first, then the model catalog). Edit it from the management page's Settings tab.

codebuddy.customModels.description: Custom model IDs to add beyond the server list

codebuddy.modelAllowlist.description: Model ids forced INTO the model list even though the catalog's curation leaves them out (whitelist). Edited by switching a greyed model on in the management page's Models tab.

codebuddy.modelBlocklist.description: Model ids forced OUT of the model list (blacklist). Applied last, so it also beats custom models and the whitelist. Edited by switching a model off in the management page's Models tab.

codebuddy.enabled.description: Offer the CodeBuddy model group to VS Code's model picker

codebuddy.autoSelectAccount.description: Allocate accounts automatically per request: prefer credits that expire soonest, keep one account per conversation for ~30 minutes of activity. An explicit account choice still wins.

codebuddy.region.description: Which cluster the management page opens on. Each region has its own sign-in, account and quota; switching here does not move accounts or spend the other cluster's credits.
